intro: Move a county property tax up or down — the county’s general fund, the sheriff’s patrol tax, the fire tax, or the schools — and see what it does to a household’s bill, to the budget, and to what that money could pay for or would have to give up. Every rate and tax base comes from a cited document.

household.homestead_label: It’s my homestead (takes off Florida’s homestead exemption)
household.where: The household example is a home in unincorporated Brevard County (outside any city), so it pays the county general fund, the sheriff’s patrol tax, the fire tax, and the schools.
household.note: Florida taxes property on its assessed value, in mills: $1 for every $1,000. Use the assessed value on your TRIM notice or bcpao.us. The homestead box takes off $51,411 for county taxes and $25,000 for school taxes (2026). Rates are the final 2025 rates. Smaller taxes on the bill (library, mosquito control, recreation, road and water districts) stay as they are; a home inside a city pays the city’s tax instead of the sheriff’s patrol tax.

layers.name: Brevard County general fund mills
layers.base_note: One mill raises about $76.4 million a year across the whole county — its 2026 taxable value is $76,403,021,129. The general fund pays for most county services, including the jail. 2.8643 is the 2025 rate; the July proposal for 2026 was 2.8625 (book p. 21), and the final rates were set by Resolution 26-090 on September 22, 2026.

caps.text: Florida’s Constitution caps county operating taxes at 10 mills (Art. VII, §9(b)).

projects.name: the jail’s yearly raise this year ($61.6M → $66.6M)
a year of the jail’s food and medical care

layers.name: Law Enforcement MSTU (unincorporated areas)
layers.base_note: Paid in the areas the Sheriff patrols — mostly unincorporated Brevard, outside the cities with their own police. One mill raises about $33.4 million: the district’s 2026 taxable value is $33,358,102,229.

layers.name: Fire Control MSTU
layers.base_note: Pays for Brevard County Fire Rescue where the county provides fire service. One mill raises about $36.5 million: the district’s 2026 taxable value is $36,455,456,846.

layers.name: Brevard Public Schools mills
layers.base_note: One mill raises about $82.9 million a year — the school district’s 2026 taxable value is $82,873,662,940. The 6.31 mills (2025) are 3.062 required by the state, 0.748 set by the School Board, 1.5 for buildings, and 1.0 that voters approved for teacher pay.

caps.text: The state sets the required mills each year; Florida law caps the School Board’s own operating levy (0.748 mills, the amount the state budget allows) and its building levy at 1.5 mills (§1011.71). Anything more needs the voters — as the teacher-pay mill did.

law.text: Florida’s Truth in Millage (TRIM) law: each August the Property Appraiser mails every owner a notice with each government’s proposed rate and its rolled-back rate; budgets are then adopted at two September hearings.
Homesteads get up to $51,411 off county and city taxes in 2026 ($25,000 off school taxes), and Save Our Homes limits a homestead’s yearly assessment increase to 3% or inflation, whichever is less.

On the November 3, 2026 ballot, Amendment 3 would raise the homestead exemption for non-school taxes to up to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, and cut the yearly cap on non-homestead assessment increases from 10% to 5%. School taxes would keep the $25,000 exemption. It needs 60% to pass. In FY2024-25, homesteads paid 41.6% of the county commission’s property taxes. This site gives facts on the amendment and takes no side.

The county’s own estimate: a $250,000 homestead exemption under Amendment 3 would reduce Brevard County property tax revenue by more than $87 million a year (26%) at current rates — $54.1 million from the General Fund, $7.3 million from the sheriff’s patrol tax, $6.0 million from fire rescue. Reported here as the county’s figure; no side taken.

limits: Tax bases are held at the 2026 certified values. Values move every year, and if Amendment 3 passes, homestead taxable values would fall sharply starting in 2027.
Not every bill gets paid on time, and early payers get up to a 4% discount; governments budget about 95–97% of the levy for that reason.
The general fund and school mills raise money from every property in the county; the sheriff’s patrol and fire taxes only from the areas they serve.
Save Our Homes means a long-time homesteader’s assessed value can be far below market value. Use the assessed value on your notice, not the sale price.
Saving-up times ignore interest earned and rising construction costs.
